Known as the "Abortomat," the locker is in a building opposite the Polish parliament, in what activists say is a clear message to politicians like Donald Tusk . stories.title: Germany gives sweeping powers to police, intelligence services
stories.summary: Drone sightings and cyberattacks have heightened security concerns. How are the police preparing to meet these challenges? And how do intelligence services plan to counter threats from both domestic and foreign sources?
stories.article_text_excerpt: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5PQR9 Prefer DW on Google Cybercrime can also affect supermarkets, like Irish chain SuperValu whose cooling systems were hacked in early November Image: REUTERS Advertisement Germany's intelligence agencies have been given wide-ranging new powers. The lawmakers in the Bundestag agreed to a reform package on Friday. Under the new rules, the Federal Intelligence Service (BND), Germany's foreign intelligence service, will be allowed to respond to cyberattacks by foreign powers with counterattacks of its own. The range of possible measures is broad, from deleting and manipulating data to disabling entire systems and, if necessary, even destroying physical weapons such as drones that could be deployed against Germany. Under certain conditions, the agencies will also be permitted to enter homes and business premises covertly, for example, to prepare surveillance operations. They will, however, not be allowed to use force against people. An independent oversight board is to be established to monitor the agencies. Opposition lawmakers specializing in domestic policy warned against granting powers that are too broad.

stories.article_text_excerpt: The European Commission will on Wednesday present a plan to provide a €45 billion loan to Ukraine backed by headroom in the bloc’s long-term budget, according to two EU officials. The loan, which would have to be agreed by EU leaders, aims to keep Ukraine financially afloat in the coming year as Moscow ramps up its drone and missile attacks against Ukrainian infrastructure. The Commission will propose that EU leaders agree to backstop the loan with the headroom in the EU’s current long-term budget, in a similar way to how a previous €90 billion loan was backed by the budget, the officials said. EU leaders are due to discuss the loan at their next gathering on Nov. 26-27. They will need to agree unanimously to use the headroom, or remaining amounts, in the Multiannual Financial Framework to finance the loan. Hungary, Slovakia, Czechia and Bulgaria have signaled they will not participate in future loans for Ukraine, but in the past these countries did not block using the MFF to backstop Ukraine loans. stories.summary: Researchers found that dementia risk increases with the number of cigarettes smoked per day, rising by 16% for those who smoke 10 a day and by 34% for those who smoke 20, compared with people who have never smoked.

stories.title: How a new ‘green energy corridor’ from the Caspian Sea could help Eastern Europe kick fossil fuels

stories.title: Turkey: Six-metre Trojan Horse spills plastic waste at COP31
stories.summary: A giant Trojan Horse overflowing with plastic waste has appeared in Antalya as Greenpeace International staged a striking environmental protest during the COP31 climate summit. Created with Danish artist Thomas Dambo, the Greenpeace installation warns of the environmental impact of plastics.

stories.title: North Macedonia: Kriva Palanka seeks help over 1,000 free-roaming cows
stories.summary: More than 1,000 cows are roaming freely through Kriva Palanka in North Macedonia, damaging property and alarming residents. The mayor wants the government to declare a 30-day state of crisis.
